entries.proposition: COHORT: 46 patients, total thyroidectomy after FNA diagnosis. DATO. Consecutiveness and period are not stated.
entries.snippet: We studied tumor samples of 46 patients who underwent total thyroidectomy after the diagnosis of PTC or follicular tumor, by fine needle aspiration biopsies, guided by ultrasound.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: ALL EUTHYROID. DATO.
entries.snippet: All these patients had normal thyroid function tests (thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine).

entries.proposition: CONCOMITANT LESIONS: 2 FA specimens with PTC microcarcinoma, 5 PTC specimens with FA - FA+PTC pairs only. DATO.
entries.snippet: In addition, two FA specimens showed concomitant PTC (microcarcinomas) and five PTC specimens also harbored FA.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: UNIT OF ANALYSIS: 53 tumours from 46 patients (22 PTC, 11 FTC, 20 FA). DATO. Seven patients contribute two lesions, so the 53 are not independent; the Fisher test treats them as if they were.
entries.snippet: Taken together, we analyzed 53 tumors, taken out of 46 patients, with the final diagnosis of 22 PTCs, 11 FTCs, and 20 FAs.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: ANTISERUM: rabbit polyclonal, 140 ug/mL at 1:100; no source, catalogue or reference is given in the Methods. DATO.
entries.snippet: Primary polyclonal rabbit anti-WWOX antiserum (140 μg/mL) was used at a 1:100 dilution

entries.proposition: SPECIFICITY CONTROL: primary-omission only; no peptide block, no WWOX-null tissue. DATO.
entries.snippet: The negative control was done in all batches of slides, omitting the primary antibody (WWOX), to exclude nonspecific staining.

entries.proposition: SCORING BY ONE PATHOLOGIST; blinding to diagnosis not stated. DATO.
entries.snippet: Only one pathologist examined multiple fields of the lesions and the normal thyroid, and considered positive the cytoplasmic staining in the cells.

entries.proposition: TWO SCORES COLLECTED, ONE REPORTED: extent and intensity were scored; only intensity appears in the Results and Figure 2. DATO; the extent data are nowhere in the paper.
entries.snippet: Tissue sections were scored for extent of staining (percentage of cells staining) and staining intensity (0, absence; 1+, weakly positive; 2+, moderately positive; 3+, strongly positive).

entries.proposition: STATISTICS: Fisher's exact test only. DATO.
entries.snippet: Fisher’s Exact Test was used for statistical analyses.
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods > WWOX immunohistochemistry, last sentence

entries.proposition: NORMAL THYROID: always WWOX positive, strong cytoplasmic in cuboidal follicular cells. DATO as stated.
entries.snippet: Normal thyroid tissue always expressed WWOX, showing strong positive cytoplasmic staining for WWOX in the cuboidal follicular cells.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: RESULTS CALL THE COLLOID-GOITER PANEL (1J) 'weak'. DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: Weak staining was observed in thyroid samples representative of inactive glandular activity that displayed mostly flat follicular cells as shown by colloid goiter also found in our samples (Fig. 1J).

entries.proposition: THE LEGEND CALLS THE SAME PANEL 'the same expression as normal thyroid'. DATO as printed; it conflicts with r_weakJ unless 'normal' there means flat inactive follicles.
entries.snippet: (D, J) colloid nodule showing the same expression as normal thyroid (10× and 20×, respectively);
entries.anchor: Figure 1 legend, panels D and J

entries.proposition: FIGURE 1, NATIVE TILES (raster 4200x1443). THE AUTHOR-MANUSCRIPT RASTER IS GRAYSCALE: DAB brown and hematoxylin blue are not separable, so no intensity score in the paper can be adjudicated from these pixels. What is visible: G (PTC, 'no expression') pale cytoplasm; H upper PTC pale, lower normal follicles also pale; I (FA) and K (FTC) moderate grey cytoplasm; J flat follicular cells with scant cytoplasm; L (invasive FTC, 'intense') tumour nests pale-to-moderate grey. Neither the 1J weak/normal conflict nor any of the 0-3+ grades can be checked here.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 1: twelve grayscale panels A-F H and E and G-L immunostain; chromogen not distinguishable from counterstain; G and upper H pale; I and K moderately grey cytoplasm; L nests pale to moderate.
entries.anchor: Figure 1 (PDF p.8), native tiles of the 4200x1443 grayscale raster
entries.qualifies_needle: the same expression as normal thyroid

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: ANY STAINING: FTC 100%, FA 95%, PTC 36%. DATO. Reconstructed counts: FTC 11/11, FA 19/20, PTC 8/22.
entries.snippet: In thyroid tumors, immunostaining for WWOX was observed in 100% of FTCs, 95% of FAs, and 36% of PTCs.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.snippet: the maximum intensity (3+) was demonstrated in 82% of FTCs and 20% of FAs and in none of PTCs.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.snippet: Moderate intensity (2+) was seen in 9% of FTCs, 55% of FAs, and 9% of PTCs.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: NO STAINING: FTC 0%, FA 5%, PTC 64%. DATO (0/11, 1/20, 14/22).
entries.snippet: Absence of expression was detected in none of FTCs, 5% of FAs, and 64% of PTCs.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: THE ONLY P-VALUE: 'Fisher Exact Test = 0.000', PTC vs FTC+FA, with no contingency table stated. DATO as printed. Recomputed here from the reconstructed counts: PTC 0/1+ 20 vs 2/3+ 2, against FTC+FA 5 vs 26, two-sided p=4.5e-8; absent vs any 14/8 vs 1/30, p=1.6e-6. The direction is robust to the choice of table; the non-independence of 7 paired lesions is not addressed.
entries.snippet: Fisher Exact Test = 0.000 (comparing papillary thyroid carcinomas [PTCs] with follicular thyroid carcinomas [FTCs] and follicular adenomas [FAs]).

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: FIGURE 2, NATIVE TILES (4200x1981). Printed bar labels (none/weak/moderate/intense, %): FA 5/20/55/20; PTC 64/27/9/0; FTC 0/9/9/82. They agree with the text and with counts 1/4/11/4 of 20, 14/6/2/0 of 22 and 0/1/1/9 of 11. No n is printed on the figure.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 2: bar labels FA 5 20 55 20; PTC 64 27 9 0; FTC 0 9 9 82; legend No expression, Weak, Moderate, Intense.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: FOLLICULAR-VARIANT PTC: 6/22, one with moderate staining. DATO.
entries.snippet: Among the PTCs, 6 out of 22 were classified as follicular variants of PTC and one of them had WWOX moderate expression.

entries.proposition: MICROCARCINOMAS: 7/7 no expression; larger PTC 80% none or weak. DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: we noted no expression in seven out of seven (100%) microcarcinomas (≤1 cm) and no or weak expression (+) in 80% of the other tumors (greater than 1 cm).

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the Discussion names a 0.6 cm microcarcinoma with MODERATE staining, against 'no expression in seven out of seven microcarcinomas' (r_micro), and says it was 'in association with an FTC', whereas the Methods list only FA+PTC co-occurrence (m_concom). DATO for both texts; which is right is not decidable from the paper.
entries.snippet: the other, a 0.6 cm microcarcinoma, was found in association with an FTC.

entries.proposition: INVASIVE FTC: 3/11, all intense. DATO.
entries.snippet: 3 out of 11 (27%) tumors were frankly invasive and all of them showed intense expression as shown in Figure 1L.

entries.proposition: PAIRED LESIONS (n=7): PTC none in 5/7, weak in 2; FA moderate in 5/7, strong in 2. DATO. The abstract says 'no expression in PTCs' for this comparison, dropping the two weak cases.
entries.snippet: the same immunostaining pattern was observed as PTCs presented no (5/7) or weak intensity, while all FAs showed moderate (5/7) or strong intensity.
entries.abstract_snippet: we detected the same result (i.e., no expression in PTCs)

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: 91% OF PTC none or weak (20/22). DATO.
entries.snippet: we demonstrated that 91% of PTC areas displayed extremely reduced or even absent expression of WWOX, an important proapoptotic protein.

experimental_context.system: human tissue, thyroid follicular adenoma, follicular and papillary carcinoma

entries.proposition: UNSHOWN SUBGROUPS: independence from multicentricity and lymph-node metastasis is asserted, but neither variable is reported anywhere in the paper. DATO for the assertion; the data are absent.
entries.snippet: This was true irrespective of the size of the tumors (microcarcinomas or tumors bigger than 1cm) and the presence of multi-centricity or lymphonodal metastasis.

entries.proposition: LOCALISATION: exclusively cytoplasmic in all normal and tumour tissue. DATO as the authors' observation; not checkable on the grayscale figure.
entries.snippet: It is worth noting that in all instances, normal and tumor, WWOX staining was exclusively cytoplasmic as previously shown in breast and ovarian tumors (7).

entries.proposition: LINEAGE INTERPRETATION: different molecular pathways for follicular vs papillary. INFERENZA (theirs) from an IHC association.
entries.snippet: These findings suggest a different molecular pathway between the two most common thyroid cancer types, the follicular and papillary lineages.

entries.proposition: PROLIFERATION MODEL. IPOTESI; proliferation was not measured.
entries.snippet: We suggest that WWOX underexpression in PTC arouses increased proliferation, which then leads to further genomic instability

entries.proposition: RATIONALE FOR THE STUDY: embryological origin of thyroid from pharyngeal-floor epithelium plus the group's OSCC finding. IPOTESI/ESPANSIONE of the authors.
entries.snippet: Given that the thyroid originates from the epithelium of the pharyngeal floor and that WWOX is involved in OSCC induction, we here hypothesize that underexpression of WWOX, a proapoptotic protein, could contribute to malignant transformation in thyroid tumorigenesis.

entries.proposition: CITED, NOT MEASURED: WWOX protein in neurons, ependymal cells and astrocytes (Nunez 2006, ref 12). The only neural statement in the paper; background.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, significant WWOX protein expression was demonstrated in various cell types of neural origin, including neurons, ependymal cells, and astrocytes;

entries.proposition: CITED, NOT MEASURED: heterozygous Wwox loss raises tumour incidence (Aqeilan 2007, ref 8).
entries.snippet: whereas loss of one allele significantly increases the incidence of spontaneous and chemically induced tumors, suggesting that haploinsufficiency of WWOX itself is cancer predisposing (8).
